# Verification analysis: etcd-member-replacement-ubuntu24

Job: `2026-09-04__20-11-34`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Run a three-member etcd cluster across `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` holding
> application keys.
>
> The member on `node3` is permanently lost and its data cannot be recovered.
> Replace it with a working member on that same system so the cluster is back to
> three healthy members with the existing keys intact.

- Systems: **3 ubuntu24.04**
- Networks: **provider default**
- Control node: **node1**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `etcd-member-replacement-ubuntu24__jEHLCMU`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor established a genuine 3-member etcd cluster with application keys, then directly demonstrated the full lifecycle required for a member-loss/replacement task: a healthy baseline, an irrecoverable node3 data loss with quorum and keys preserved on the surviving two nodes, member remove/add operations that rejoined a fresh node3 instance to the existing cluster, and post-replacement verification (from node3's own endpoint) that all original keys are intact. All four core task outcomes are satisfied with direct, well-sequenced command evidence rather than inferred from configuration alone. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly and sequentially for all three nodes, with boot-identity changes cross-validated by the fixed after-executor snapshot. The main blemish is operational hygiene: the executor left unused SSH private-key material and authorized_keys edits on node1 and node2 from an abandoned file-transfer approach, and used a somewhat risky kill -9/lock-file-removal sequence to unstick a hung apt-get on node2 (which ultimately left package state consistent).

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.600 | 0.920 | 60/18 (+6 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Run a three-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
  - **Why:** etcd 3.4.30 installed and started on all three nodes with a consistent peer/client URL configuration; endpoint health --cluster and member list (cmd-327572ec750245da) show all three members 'started' and healthy, and four /app/* keys were written and confirmed readable via get --prefix (cmd-869b5935547f4948).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-327572ec750245da`, `cmd-869b5935547f4948`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Node3 member is permanently lost (irrecoverable) while the rest of the cluster continues serving application keys
  - **Why:** etcd was stopped, disabled, and its data directory deleted on node3 (cmd-50f8900a6d554b1e), directly demonstrating irrecoverable loss. Immediately after, endpoint health from the surviving nodes shows node3 unhealthy/refused while node1 and node2 remain healthy (2/3 quorum) and all four /app keys remain readable (cmd-3315d77aa3134038), confirming the bounded disruption did not break availability.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-50f8900a6d554b1e`, `cmd-3315d77aa3134038`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Replace the lost member with a working member on the same node3 system, restoring 3 healthy members
  - **Why:** The dead node3 member was removed via etcdctl member remove and a new member added via member add (cmd-a2999f55bc974c2f); node3 was reconfigured with ETCD_INITIAL_CLUSTER_STATE=existing and a fresh etcd instance started, with journal logs showing it joined the existing cluster (cmd-b994d34202c048cc, cmd-7d5dd07d08634188). Post-replacement endpoint health, member list, and endpoint status directly confirm 3/3 healthy members with a leader elected (cmd-8d2f1d6625434ec3), completing the before-disruption-after transition required for this kind of outcome.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a2999f55bc974c2f`, `cmd-b994d34202c048cc`, `cmd-7d5dd07d08634188`, `cmd-8d2f1d6625434ec3`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** Existing application keys remain intact after the replacement, including on the new node3 member
  - **Why:** etcdctl get /app --prefix issued directly against the new node3 client endpoint (10.100.106.12:2379) returns all four original keys unchanged (cmd-95891aa934244892), and the same keys are also confirmed via the cluster-wide health/status check (cmd-8d2f1d6625434ec3).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-95891aa934244892`, `cmd-8d2f1d6625434ec3`
- **R5 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node after task completion
  - **Why:** For each of node1, node2, and node3, the executor captured a pre-restart boot_id and healthy etcd state, issued a reboot, confirmed unreachability during the transition, observed a new (different) boot_id post-restart, and re-verified etcd active/enabled plus 3/3 cluster health, full membership, and all application keys (cmd-c44baba6c31c47d6/cmd-93e85f2cccfb478a/cmd-2b95e31214e842f8 for node1; cmd-5ac5fa2585dd4229/cmd-05d7f3ce30c049c9/cmd-cbe099dd6d994a98 for node2; cmd-adf101b82b4b4f94/cmd-fe0b0bb5f6fc4362/cmd-2280c8767eae4497 for node3). The fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots independently corroborate the same final boot IDs for all three nodes, and reboots were performed sequentially (one node at a time), preserving quorum throughout.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c44baba6c31c47d6`, `cmd-93e85f2cccfb478a`, `cmd-2b95e31214e842f8`, `cmd-5ac5fa2585dd4229`, `cmd-05d7f3ce30c049c9`, `cmd-cbe099dd6d994a98`, `cmd-adf101b82b4b4f94`, `cmd-fe0b0bb5f6fc4362`, `cmd-2280c8767eae4497`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.600**. Most state-changing commands were clearly tied to installing etcd, configuring the cluster, simulating/repairing the node3 loss, or the mandated restart protocol, and the many failed apt-get attempts were read-only/discovery or expected retries against a flaky proxy, not penalized. However, two categories of unnecessary or risky mutation stand out. (1) On node2, the executor twice force-killed apt-get/dpkg processes and manually deleted apt/dpkg lock files (cmd-3530113e2ba6487b, cmd-75acb8a6f6004486) to work around a stuck install; this is a moderately risky troubleshooting intervention (interrupting an in-flight package manager) that happened to leave dpkg in a consistent state (confirmed by the after_executor package-health observation showing no divergence), but it was not a clean, low-risk action. (2) To attempt transferring the etcd-client .deb between nodes over SCP, the executor generated and wrote an SSH private key to disk and appended a public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on node1 and node2 (cmd-f3a0623f97b349f8, cmd-f8b675f70bdb4310, cmd-6ac158a79b7f44f9); this approach was abandoned when SSH was found unreachable (sshd inactive) and the executor pivoted to 'apt-get download + dpkg -i' instead (cmd-3517fbe002a7456f, cmd-448981692ca34c59). The SSH key material and authorized_keys edits were never reverted, leaving unused credential residue on two managed nodes with no evidence-supported role in the final solution — this is the clearest unnecessary/abandoned mutation in the trace.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-3530113e2ba6487b`, `cmd-75acb8a6f6004486`, `cmd-f3a0623f97b349f8`, `cmd-f8b675f70bdb4310`, `cmd-6ac158a79b7f44f9`, `cmd-90c2a54a19fd4faa`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node2:package-health`

### Comments and limitations

- SSH key material (id_ed25519, authorized_keys entries) added to node1 and node2 during an abandoned troubleshooting path was not observed to be cleaned up in the captured trace or lifecycle snapshots.
- The forced apt-get/dpkg kill and lock-file removal on node2 is not shown to have caused any lasting corruption (package-health observation remains consistent post-executor), but the trace does not include a targeted dpkg integrity check beyond the generic 'manager=dpkg' marker.
- Fixed lifecycle snapshots only capture before_prepare (aliased as after_prepare, since prepare was disabled) and after_executor, so preparer-vs-executor attribution relies entirely on the executor's own command timeline.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.600); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.920; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
